Canonical Correlation Analysis via SVD

Source: R/cca.R
run_cca.Rd

Computes CCA between two matrices using the standard whitening + SVD formulation, implemented in base R. Intended as a drop-in replacement for CCA::rcc() within kstitch: the return value mirrors the structure of CCA::cc() / CCA::rcc() ($cor, $xcoef, $ycoef, and a $scores list holding the canonical variates and the structure-correlation blocks), so downstream code that consumes those fields needs no other changes.

run_cca(X, Y, scale = TRUE, tol = 1e-08)

Arguments

X

Numeric matrix (cells x features), e.g. the shape / morphology matrix. Rownames should be cell IDs and colnames feature names.

Y

Numeric matrix (cells x features), e.g. the NMF factor matrix. Must have the same rows (cells) as X.

scale

Logical; if TRUE (default) the columns of X and Y are standardized (centered and scaled to unit variance) before the analysis. If FALSE the matrices are used as supplied (still centered internally for the covariance computation). Classical CCA is invariant to per-column rescaling, so this mainly affects numerical conditioning and the interpretation of the weight vectors, not the canonical correlations.

tol

Eigenvalues below this threshold are clamped before inversion, to guard against numerical blow-up during whitening of a near-singular covariance matrix.

Value

A list with components:

cor

Canonical correlations, length K = min(ncol(X), ncol(Y)).

xcoef, ycoef

Canonical weight vectors (features x K).

scores

List with xscores, yscores (canonical variates, cells x K) plus structure correlations corr.X.xscores, corr.Y.xscores, corr.X.yscores, corr.Y.yscores.
